problems.name: Fibonacci Number
problems.question: Given n, return the nth Fibonacci number where F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, and F(n) = F(n - 1) + F(n - 2).
problems.constraints: 0 <= n <= 30 in the original problem; use int for the original range.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative DP keeps only the previous two values.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion computes each n once and uses call stack plus memo.

problems.name: Climbing Stairs
problems.question: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each move can climb 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative DP keeps the last two counts.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Memoized recursion stores each step count once.

problems.name: Pow(x, n)
problems.question: Implement pow(x, n), which calculates x raised to the power n.
problems.constraints: -100.0 < x < 100.0; -2147483648 <= n <= 2147483647; result fits standard double constraints.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(log |n|); Space O(1). Iterative binary exponentiation halves the exponent.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(log |n|); Space O(log |n|). Recursive fast power halves the exponent at each call.

problems.name: Reverse String
problems.question: Given a character array s, reverse it in-place.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100000; s[i] is a printable ASCII character in the original problem.

examples.explanation: Case is preserved while positions change.
A single character is already reversed.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative two pointers swap in-place.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n) call stack. Recursive two pointers swap one pair per call.

problems.name: Swap Nodes in Pairs
problems.question: Given a linked list, swap every two adjacent nodes and return its head. Node values must not be modified.

examples.explanation: There are no nodes to swap.
The final unpaired node remains in place.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Iterative pointer rewiring uses a dummy node.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n) call stack. Each call swaps one pair.

problems.name: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problems.question: Given the heads of two sorted linked lists, merge them into one sorted linked list and return its head.
problems.constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each list <= 50; -100 <= Node.val <= 100; both lists are sorted nondecreasing.

examples.explanation: Nodes are merged in sorted order.
The non-empty list is already the answer.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(m+n); Space O(1). Iteratively relink existing nodes.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(m+n); Space O(m+n) call stack. Each call consumes one node.

problems.name: K-th Symbol in Grammar
problems.question: In row 1 the grammar is 0. Each 0 becomes 01 and each 1 becomes 10. Return the kth symbol in row n.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Count flips while walking from k toward the root.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Recursively ask for the parent symbol.

problems.name: Generate Parentheses
problems.question: Given n pairs of parentheses, generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.

examples.explanation: All valid strings with three pairs are generated.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(Cn * n); Space O(Cn * n). Iterative stack explores only valid prefixes, where Cn is the nth Catalan number.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(Cn * n); Space O(n) call stack excluding output. Recursion prunes invalid prefixes early.

problems.name: Subsets
problems.question: Given an integer array nums with unique elements, return all possible subsets of nums.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 10; -10 <= nums[i] <= 10; all nums values are unique.

examples.explanation: A single element can be excluded or included.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n * 2^n). Iteratively extend previous subsets.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n); Space O(n) recursion stack excluding output. Include-exclude recursion creates every subset.

problems.name: Permutations
problems.question: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all possible permutations.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 6; -10 <= nums[i] <= 10; all nums values are unique.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n! * n); Space O(n! * n). Iterative insertion builds permutations level by level.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n! * n); Space O(n) recursion stack excluding output. Backtracking chooses unused values.

problems.name: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
problems.question: Given a string digits containing digits 2 through 9, return all possible letter combinations the number could represent.

examples.explanation: Every letter from 2 combines with every letter from 3.
Digit 2 maps to a, b, and c.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(4^n * n); Space O(4^n * n). Queue expansion processes combinations level by level.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(4^n * n); Space O(n) call stack excluding output. Backtracking builds one string at a time.

problems.name: Combinations
problems.question: Given integers n and k, return all possible combinations of k numbers chosen from the range 1 to n.

examples.explanation: All size-2 choices from 1..4 are returned.
Choosing all numbers gives one combination.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(C(n,k) * k); Space O(k) stack state excluding output. Iterative stack simulates increasing choices.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(C(n,k) * k); Space O(k) call stack excluding output. Pruned recursion builds only valid-size paths.

problems.name: Combination Sum
problems.question: Given distinct candidate numbers and a target, return all unique combinations where chosen numbers sum to target. A candidate may be chosen unlimited times.
problems.constraints: 1 <= candidates.length <= 30; 2 <= candidates[i] <= 40; all candidates are distinct; 1 <= target <= 40.

examples.explanation: 2 can be reused and 7 is an exact match.
All unique combinations summing to 8 are returned.
No candidate can sum to the target.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time exponential in output size; Space O(target/minCandidate). Iterative stack stores partial combinations and remaining sums.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time exponential in output size; Space O(target/minCandidate). Backtracking prunes when candidate exceeds remaining target.

problems.name: N-Queens
problems.question: Given n, return all distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle, placing n queens on an n x n chessboard so no two queens attack each other.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n!); Space O(n). Iterative stack tracks row choices and constraint sets.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n!); Space O(n). Recursive backtracking places one queen per row with O(1) safety checks.

problems.name: Sudoku Solver
problems.question: Write a program to solve a 9 x 9 Sudoku board by filling empty cells marked with dot characters.
problems.constraints: board.length == 9; board[i].length == 9; board contains digits 1..9 or dot; the input has exactly one solution.

examples.explanation: Every row, column, and 3x3 box is filled with digits 1 through 9.
Only the valid digit is placed.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(9^e) worst case with faster O(1) validity checks; Space O(e). Iterative stack uses bit masks.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(9^e) worst case with O(1) validity checks; Space O(e). Recursive backtracking fills one blank per level.

problems.name: Word Search
problems.question: Given an m x n board of characters and a word, return true if the word exists in the grid by moving horizontally or vertically without reusing a cell.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m, n <= 6; 1 <= word.length <= 15; board and word contain uppercase/lowercase English letters in the original problem.

examples.explanation: A valid adjacent path spells the word.
The word can be formed on the right side.
The path would need to reuse B.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(m*n*3^L); Space O(L). Iterative DFS avoids immediately revisiting the previous path cells.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(m*n*3^L); Space O(L). Recursive backtracking marks cells in-place during the path.

problems.name: Same Tree
problems.question: Given the roots of two binary trees p and q, return true if they are structurally identical and node values are equal.
problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(w). Iterative stack or queue compares node pairs.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(h). Recursive DFS compares corresponding subtrees.

problems.name: Symmetric Tree
problems.question: Given the root of a binary tree, return true if it is symmetric around its center.

examples.explanation: The left and right sides mirror each other.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(w). Iterative queue compares mirror pairs.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(h). Recursive mirror comparison follows opposite branches.

problems.name: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
problems.question: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth.

examples.explanation: The longest root-to-leaf path has 3 nodes.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(w). BFS counts levels iteratively.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(h). Recursive DFS returns height from children.

problems.name: Invert Binary Tree
problems.question: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree and return its root.

examples.explanation: Every left and right child pair is swapped.
The two children of the root swap.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(w). Iterative BFS swaps every node once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(h). Recursive DFS swaps current node and subtrees.
